text:
Maya: FYI saw a hard OOM on node-34 at 03:12 UTC during the last load test. Dump + perf sample uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/dumps/2067894321-node34-oom.gz :frowning:

Jon: @Maya can you paste the failing batch shape? I suspect KV-heavy requests + one long seq forcing kernel fallback is the culprit.

Maya: Batch had 6 reqs, tokens [12, 8, 1024, 16, 20, 64], inflight tokens ~1204. KV entries per req: [0, 2, 46, 0, 1, 3]. Hot req was the 1024 seq with KV depth 46.

Rachel: Profiling shows kv_alloc spike ~3.1GB and we saw kernel fallback to nvcc_attention_fallback around the same time. Flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/trace/2067894321 :eyes: CPU sched churn too.

Steve: This matches past incidents. Problem is mixing one very long sequence + deep KV inside the same batch; admission currently only counts tokens (token_budget=2048). We need admission to account for KV memory pressure, not just token counts.

Steve: Proposal: compute kv_penalty per-request and treat it as extra token-equivalent when admitting. effective_req_tokens = tokens + ceil(kv_penalty / token_byte_equiv). Admit only when sum(effective_req_tokens) <= batch_budget.

Steve: quick pseudo: ```python
KV_ENTRY_BYTES = 128  # estimate
TOKEN_BYTES = 8
kv_penalty = req.kv_entries * KV_ENTRY_BYTES
effective = req.tokens + (kv_penalty + TOKEN_BYTES - 1) // TOKEN_BYTES
if total_effective + effective <= BATCH_BUDGET:
    accept
else:
    defer
```

Kris: Also factor kernel_cost: some kernels (long-attn) allocate temporaries. If kernel_cost > 1.0 then scale effective by kernel_cost so admission avoids combos that trigger heavy temporaries.

Jon: Runtime knobs we can expose: batch_budget_tokens, batch_kv_bytes_budget, kernel_scale_factors, and single_request_isolation_threshold. Short-term mitigation: set batch_kv_bytes_budget=1GB and reduce batch_window to 20ms to avoid creating giant mixed batches.

Rachel: Ran a staging sim with budgeted admission and kernel scaling: OOMs dropped to 0 for the same workload. Trade-offs: median latency +12ms, p99 +40ms, throughput ~-2%. Acceptable compared to outages.

Maya: What about a single request that itself exceeds the kv budget (the 46-entry one)? We need a fallback to avoid it blocking everything.

Steve: Add single_request_isolation when req.kv_bytes > batch_kv_bytes_budget * 0.6: run alone on a slot. Also consider evictable_prefix_compaction for prefix-like KV entries to reduce active footprint.

Kris: Prototype idea: probabilistic soft-eviction when queue backlog > N: pick infrequently-used KV pages and temporarily drop them (mark + restore on completion). It's risky but could buy headroom for tail events.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by @Jon: feature/budgeted-admission -> staging at 2026-03-17T04:00Z :rocket:

Jon: I'll run an extended soak tonight and capture KV footprint per-slot and per-kernel. @Rachel can you add a regression alert for p99 latency when kv_bytes > 80% of budget?

Rachel: Added alert to #alerts:kv-batches and updated dashboard: /dash/kv_admission/2067894321.

Maya: Thanks team. Next steps: Jon run soak, Steve add kernel_scale, Kris prototype soft-evict POC, Rachel monitor. Filing follow-up ticket INF-4127. :thumbsup:
